raw_response:
I been farming this land 30 years. I do same as last year because last year was alright. My neighbors all do similar — we plant wheat after October, then maize right after wheat comes off in June. Land never rests, that's how we do here.

For wheat — I buy two bags of fertilizer per mu before planting, the kind with three numbers (compound). One bag is 50 jin… no wait, one bag is 100 jin (50 kg). I put it down when I rotary-till the field. Then in spring when wheat starts standing up tall, I broadcast urea, maybe 30-40 jin per mu, before the rain or before I water. I water three times — once before deep winter so roots don't dry out, once at jointing with the urea, once when grain is filling. If I see yellow leaves or worms I spray, usually twice in the season. My wheat gives me around 950 jin per mu most years (475 kg). I plant the variety the seed shop sells — most everyone in our village uses the same one, Jimai I think they call it.

For maize — after wheat harvest I don't plough, no time. I direct-seed with the machine, hybrid seed from the dealer. Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever they have. I put compound fertilizer down with the seeder, then when maize is knee-high I topdress urea. I water once or twice depending on the rain — if July rains good I only water once at tasseling. Spray once for borer and armyworm. Maize gives me around 1100 jin (550 kg) per mu, sometimes more if weather good.

I don't measure exact, I go by the bag. Two bags compound + one and half bags urea on wheat. One bag compound + one bag urea on maize. Costs me maybe 200-250 yuan per mu each crop for fertilizer. I'd rather put a little extra than have hungry crop — losing yield hurts more than the few yuan extra fertilizer.
